title: Graph
description: A typed, directed graph of Amasario entities and relationships, with its own completeness metadata. The graph is directed by definition because relationship semantics are directional; an undirected view is a consumer-side projection and must not be serialised as if it were the model. Nodes are typed by the shared entity kinds and edges carry the full relationship record, so a consumer reconstructing provenance from a graph never has to consult a second document.

id.description: Identifier for this graph within the producing document.

nodes.description: The graph's nodes. May be empty for a graph whose analysis found nothing, which is a legitimate result and distinct from a failed analysis.

boundary.description: The observation boundary the graph was assembled at.

metadata.description: Structural facts about this graph, recorded by the producer so that a consumer does not have to recompute them and cannot silently disagree about them.

directed.description: Whether the graph's edges are directed. Must be true: Amasario relationship semantics are directional, so a graph that reports false is not an Amasario graph.

cyclic.description: Whether the graph contains at least one cycle. Cycles are permitted and reported rather than removed, because removing them would hide real topology.

maxDepth.description: The traversal depth the graph was bounded by, when it was bounded.

truncated.description: Whether traversal stopped before exhausting the reachable graph.

disconnectedNodes.description: Identifiers of nodes with no edges. Reported explicitly because a node that was discovered but could not be related is a finding in itself, and dropping it would make the graph look tidier than the analysis was.

node.description: A typed entity in the graph.

id.description: The node identifier, which must match the identifier used when the entity is referenced from an edge in this graph.

kind.description: The entity kind. References the shared enumeration in provenance.schema.json, so node kinds and entity references can never disagree about the vocabulary.

label.description: A human-readable label for reporting. Never used for matching.

digest.description: The content digest of the node's entity, where one exists.

attributes.description: A closed set of optional structural facts about the node. Deliberately closed rather than an open bag: a fact that matters must be modelled, and a fact that is not modelled must not be smuggled in as a string.

external.description: Whether the node lies outside the observable Amasario boundary. Marked explicitly so that an uninspectable entity is never mistaken for an unverified one.

edge.description: A typed relationship in the graph, carrying the same fields as a dependency edge so that graph and dependency views cannot diverge.

source.description: The identifier of the source node. Must resolve to a node in this graph, which is enforced by rule dependency/direct-dependency and by the cross-reference integrity tests.

target.description: The identifier of the target node. Must resolve to a node in this graph.

relationship.description: The typed relationship, constrained to relationship-types.

observed.description: Whether the edge was directly observed rather than inferred.
